title: Zone augments: rewards and specialties
summary: Every top-quality augment, its drop zone and secondary specialty.
body:
Live testing: the November6 release broadens augment drops, adds balanced secondary specialties and replaces armor/default icons with stock gems/crystals/orbs. Owner approved the artwork; gameplay and balance acceptance remain open.

Drops and progression

The release uses a 1.5% augment roll on any unowned, killable NPC in an enabled reward zone, including guards, named/quest enemies, killable merchants and scripted combat adds. Player-owned pets, mercenaries, restored corpses and protected noncombat actors do not qualify. Corpse ownership and encounter access still apply. The existing equipment allowlist is separate.

Base / Polished / Exalted / Ascension weights remain 60% / 30% / 8% / 2%. That is about one augment per 67 kills, or one direct Ascension per 3,333 kills on average; forging offers the other route. Random drops have no guarantee. Chapterhouse and the Ashen Compact move from 0.5% to 1.5% within their managed expeditions. The release enables the already accessible Classic Cazic-Thule and newer Hate layout pools. Six access-check pools remain disabled.

Secondary bonuses

Existing primary stats, heroics, required levels and six type-22 armor socket locations remain. Specialty budgets at Ascension are Avoidance +4, Accuracy +5, Shielding +1%, Spell Shielding +2%, Spell Damage or Healing Amount up to +8 per augment (existing higher values retained). Six identical copies therefore add at most 24 Avoidance, 30 Accuracy, 6% Shielding, 12% Spell Shielding or 48 raw damage/healing. Existing item caps, other equipment, AAs and buffs still matter.

Shield block is distinct from Shielding: designated families add +1% at Polished/Exalted or +2% at Ascension, with only the strongest Hunt shield-block augment counted. A usable shield is required. Dodge families use Improved Dodge I from Exalted onward; the strongest worn dodge effect applies, rather than adding six copies. Spell haste and mana preservation unlock minor stock focus at Polished and full Spell Haste III / Mana Preservation III at Ascension. Stock limits and strongest-focus behavior apply: haste is 15% at the top with a three-second minimum cast, mana preservation rolls 1–10%, and both use the stock level-60 limit. Four utility families gain Faerune at Ascension (breathing, vision and see invisibility).

Recognizable drops

All four qualities in a family use a stock gem, crystal or orb icon. The old cloth gloves and default necklace are replaced. No client artwork download is needed; visible loot and inspection checks remain part of release QA.

Release checks

Guard drops, scripted adds, expedition corpse recovery, shield/dodge/focus stacking, full loot bags, forging and visible icons require in-game QA before acceptance. Existing live Hunt and encounter balance acceptance remains separate.

Equipped bonuses and stacking

Open Inventory → Stats to see your current server-calculated equipped bonuses and caps. Values update automatically while the tab is open. Shield Block and the relative Dodge modifier have their own rows. Scroll down for item spell-haste and mana-preservation potential and worn Faerune. Focus values are the best equipped item potential before spell limits; they are not a promise for every cast. The separate Shielding row remains melee damage reduction. Damage/healing caps include earned headroom. Bagged and training items give no bonus.

After fully exiting EverQuest, use launcher Play to install signed update2026110604 (client0.13.4). A missing or stale server reply shows “--”. #augstats remains a diagnostic fallback. Native sizing, scrolling and gameplay acceptance remain live QA.

Polished and Exalted Hunt shield-block augments give +1 percentage point; Ascension gives +2. Only the strongest applies. Repeated HP, mana, attributes and numeric item stats add within caps. Repeated identical spell focuses, Improved Dodge I and Faerune do not multiply the same effect. Spell focuses retain their spell/level/cast-time limits.

Shield Block is a shield-gated chance to block an attack. Shielding reduces melee damage and uses a different stat. Bagged augments and Power Source training items give no active bonuses. The native sheet may show stock caps; #augstats shows this server’s actual equipped totals and earned damage/healing headroom. Visible rendering and gameplay acceptance remain in live testing.

Shield Block shows one total including equipped augment bonuses. The strongest augment shield-block bonus applies; two +1% copies still give +1%. Shielding remains a separate damage-reduction stat.

Socketed equipment icons

The gem artwork describes the augment itself. Socketing an ordinary stat augment keeps the host equipment's own icon and appearance. Report older affected equipment.

Classic raid augments are in development. The level-50 trophies compete for one chest socket.
